cards.text: The Israelites have just set out from the Wilderness of Sinai, led by Moses, Israel's leader, with the ark of the LORD going ahead of them (Numbers 10:12, 33). Soon the people start complaining about their hardship, right in the hearing of the LORD. That's griping about your job on a call you FORGOT to mute.

cards.question: The LORD hears the people complaining, and His anger is kindled. What does He send among them at the outskirts of the camp?
The outskirts of the camp are burning. Who do the people cry out to?
Moses prays to the LORD, and the fire spreads through the whole camp.

cards.text: The fire dies down. That place gets the name Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.

Meanwhile, the rabble among them have a strong craving for other food, and again the Israelites start weeping. Friend, I know craving: that's me with my face pressed to the oven glass while the chocolate chip cookies take their sweet time.

cards.question: The Israelites are weeping and asking who will feed them. What do they want?

cards.text: Then they say they remember the fish they ate freely in Egypt, along with the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic. Friend, they're weeping over GARLIC.

cards.question: The people say their appetite is gone and there's nothing to see out here but the manna.

cards.text: Now about that manna. It resembled coriander seed, and the people gathered it, ground it or crushed it, then boiled it or shaped it into cakes.

cards.question: Friend, this is the part I've been waiting for. What did the manna taste like?
When the ___ fell on the camp at night, the manna would fall with it.

cards.text: Then Moses hears it: family after family, weeping at the entrances to their tents. And the anger of the LORD is kindled greatly.

cards.question: Family after family is weeping at their tents, and the LORD's anger is kindled greatly. Moses is ___ too.

cards.text: So Moses takes it to the LORD. He asks why the LORD has brought this trouble on His servant and laid the burden of all these people on him.

cards.question: Moses asks the LORD if he gave birth to all these people. What does Moses say he's being told to carry them like?

cards.text: Then Moses asks the LORD, "Where can I get meat for all these people?" Chip, one of my cookie cutter kids, used to beg me for one more story every night, and I thought THAT was pressure.

cards.question: Moses tells the LORD he can carry all these people by himself.
I think Moses is about as low as a man gets here. What does Moses ask the LORD to do if this is how the LORD is going to treat him?

cards.text: Then the LORD answers. He tells Moses to bring Him seventy of the elders of Israel, known leaders and officers, and have them stand with him at the Tent of Meeting.

cards.question: The LORD says He'll take some of the Spirit that is on Moses and put it on those seventy elders. What will they do?

answers.text: Help Moses bear the burden of the people
Gather the manna for the whole camp
Carry the ark ahead of the people

cards.text: Then the LORD gives Moses a message for the people: consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you will eat meat. Friend, careful what you cry out for.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses the people will eat meat for only a day or two.

cards.text: It'll be a whole month, the LORD says, until it comes out of their nostrils and makes them nauseous. Friend, that's not a portion size anymore, that's a CONSEQUENCE.

cards.question: The LORD says all that meat is coming because the people have ___ the LORD, who is among them.

cards.text: But Moses replies, "Here I am among 600,000 men on foot…" Six HUNDRED THOUSAND, and they're supposed to eat meat for a MONTH.

cards.question: Moses wonders whether slaughtering all their flocks and herds, or catching all the fish in the sea, would even be enough.

cards.text: The LORD answers Moses with a question: "Is the LORD's arm too short? Now you will see whether or not My word will come to pass."
So Moses goes out and tells the people the words of the LORD. Then he gathers seventy of the elders and has them stand around the tent.

cards.question: The LORD comes down in the cloud and places some of the Spirit that was on Moses on the seventy elders. As the Spirit rests on them, what do they do?
The seventy elders go on prophesying again and again after that day.

cards.text: But two men, Eldad and Medad, had stayed back in the camp. They were among those listed but never went out to the tent, like two names on a meeting invite who never show up.

cards.question: Even back in the camp, nowhere near the tent, the Spirit rests on Eldad and Medad.

cards.text: A young man runs to Moses with the news. Then Joshua son of Nun, Moses' attendant since youth, speaks up.

cards.question: Joshua hears that Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp. What does he tell Moses to do?
Moses asks Joshua if he's jealous on his account. Then Moses says he wishes all the LORD's people were ___.

cards.text: Moses heads back to the camp with the elders of Israel. Now a wind sent by the LORD comes up and drives in quail from the sea.

cards.question: The wind brings the quail down near the camp, about two cubits above the ground. How far out from the camp do they cover?

answers.text: A day's journey in every direction
A stone's throw on just one side
Only the ground around the tent

cards.question: The people gather the quail for just one morning and then go back to their tents.

cards.text: All that day and night and all the next day, nobody gathers less than ten homers, and they spread the quail out all around the camp. I've pulled some long nights at the ovens, friend, but never a pile like THAT.

cards.question: While the meat is still between their teeth, before it's even chewed, the anger of the LORD burns against the people. What does the LORD strike them with?
They call that place Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had ___ other food.

cards.text: From Kibroth-hattaavah, the people move on to Hazeroth. And there they stay for some time.
